ai.summary: SDK 0.4.3 introduces `stripToolCallPayloads` and exports `processToolCallBuffer` to filter `<codebuff_tool_call>` segments from non-streamed text. CLI `use-send-message` now consumes the shared SDK helper instead of local buffering logic, preventing XML leakage in final message blocks. `message-block.tsx` render keys simplified to stable IDs, removing content-length/stream-state dependencies. `run.ts` applies sanitization to accumulated text and hardens `agentId` property checks.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question and a tool runs behind the scenes, the program used to sometimes show you the hidden instruction text (the part that tells the tool what to do) mixed in with the readable answer. Starting with version 0.4.3 on October 17, 2025, that instruction text is now stripped out before the reply reaches your screen, whether the response comes all at once or in pieces. You will see cleaner message replies without any leftover command codes leaking into the conversation, and this fix now applies consistently across the whole CLI and SDK instead of relying on separate filtering in the chat display.

ai.title: Pass agent definitions to Buffbench trace and meta analyzers
ai.summary: Buffbench evals now inject full agent definitions and type references into trace and meta-analyzer contexts. The agent-runner accepts pre-loaded definitions instead of fetching them per-commit, while run-buffbench loads them once from .agents. This enables analyzers to correlate agent behavior with specific configurations, tools, and prompts. New meta-analyzer.ts aggregates cross-task performance insights.

eli5.text: The system that automatically tests your AI coding assistant now gives the evaluation tools a snapshot of how your agent is configured (its tools, prompts, and settings) right from the start of each test run. Previously, each check-up point had to pull that information separately, which meant the analysis could miss the full picture of why an agent acted a certain way. Now a single check evaluates how well one agent performs across many different tasks and highlights its strengths and weaknesses, giving a clearer report on how your assistant behaves overall.

ai.title: SDK run.ts emits buffered text mid-run
ai.summary: The `run` function in `sdk/src/run.ts` now emits accumulated text sections immediately upon receiving non-text chunks (like tool calls) or agent switches, rather than waiting for the final flush. This is achieved by introducing `emitPendingSection` and `sectionStartIndexByAgent` to track and slice buffered text for each agent key. The change ensures that intermediate text generated by subagents or preceding tool calls is visible to the `handleEvent` consumer in real-time. Tests for this behavior are added in `sdk/src/__tests__/run-text-emission.test.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run an AI assistant that uses helper agents, you'll now see the helper's written replies show up on your screen as they happen, instead of all at once at the very end. Previously, the system held onto any text written by subagents or before a tool call until the entire run finished, so the display waited. The system now tracks where each agent's current text section starts and flushes that pending text to your view the moment it encounters a tool call or switches to another agent. You'd notice helper-written text appearing live in real-time during a run today, backed by new tests covering this behavior.

ai.title: CI test matrix includes web and agent-runtime packages
ai.summary: CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` updated to add `web` and `packages/agent-runtime` to the test and integration test matrices. Previously these packages were excluded from automated test runs. This change ensures code changes in these packages trigger appropriate test jobs.

eli5.text: When someone edits code in the web interface or the agent runtime tools, those changes will now be caught by automated tests before they go live, instead of passing straight through unchecked. The test system was set up to run checks on a few packages but skipped these two areas; now it watches them too. Developers working on the web UI or the agent runtime will notice their pull requests getting additional test results, and any mistakes they introduce in those parts will be flagged automatically rather than missed.

ai.summary: Updated completions.test.ts to assert against NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL instead of hardcoded localhost. Fixes flaky test caused by environment mismatch.

eli5.text: When a credit card with insufficient funds tries to pay for a service, you now see a message that points to your actual billing address instead of a hardcoded test address that only existed on a developer's computer. Developers had set their automated payment checks to look for the wrong address, so the test would break whenever it ran in a different environment. Fixing where the test looks means the payment-failure message is now verified against the real address customers actually visit.

ai.title: Fix text block aggregation and extend streaming coverage
ai.summary: Corrects text block aggregation by removing premature state resets and enforcing trimmed text emission. Streaming coverage extends to flush pending sections specifically when active tags and partial text exist. Changes isolated to sdk/src/run.ts.

eli5.text: When you stream a response from an AI assistant, the text now shows up in clean, complete chunks instead of broken pieces, because the system stopped cutting off and restarting sections of text mid-stream. If an assistant is building up its answer while also handling tool-use tags, the system now flushes those pending sections only when it actually has meaningful text to send. You would notice fewer jarring interruptions and less empty or garbled text appearing in the middle of a streamed answer. This is live today for anyone using streaming responses.
